verses.zh: 过了五天，大祭司亚拿尼亚同几个长老，和一个辩士帖土罗下来，向巡抚控告保罗。
verses.en: After five days the high priest Ananias[NOTE:1] came down with some elders and an attorney[NOTE:2] named[NOTE:3] Tertullus, and they[NOTE:4] brought formal charges[NOTE:5] against Paul to the governor.
notes: Ananias was in office from a.d. 47-59.
The term refers to a professional advocate (BDAG 905 s.v. ῥήτωρ).
Grk “an attorney, a certain Tertullus.”

Grk “who” (plural). Because in English the relative pronoun “who” could be understood to refer only to the attorney Tertullus and not to the entire group, it has been replaced with the third person plural pronoun “they.” “And” has been supplied to provide the connection to the preceding clause.
BDAG 326 s.v. ἐμφανίζω 3 has “ἐ. τινὶ κατά τινος bring formal charges against someone…Ac 24:1; 25:2.”
verses.commentary:
24:1 "the high priest Ananias" He was high priest from A.D. 47-59. See full note at Acts 23:2. Wow!
The high priest himself came from Jerusalem to Caesarea. Paul was really a thorn in their flesh!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SADDUCEES

▣ "came down" For Jews, Jerusalem is always "up" (an idiom to accentuate the temple) and all
other geographical locations are "down."

▣ "elders" In the OT this term referred to older tribal leaders. By the post-exilic time it
began to be used of wealthy, influential people of Jerusalem. Often in the NT the Sanhedrin is described
as "the High Priests, scribes, and elders." These were probably members of the Sanhedrin who were supporters
of the Sadducees. The temple leadership had seen the potential problem when Pharisees were present
(cf. Acts 23:6-10), so they came to Caesarea without them..

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDER

SPECIAL TOPIC: SANHEDRIN

▣ "Tertullus" This was a hired lawyer (advocate) or orator (cf. NKJV). It is a form of the
Greek word rēma or "spoken word." Apparently he presented the Sanhedrin's case in an acceptable
Roman legal form, possibly in Latin.

For more information on the legal system of Rome, see A. N. Sherwin-White, Roman Society
and Roman Law in the New Testament.

verses.zh: 保罗被提了来，帖土罗就告他说：
verses.en: When Paul[NOTE:1] had been summoned, Tertullus began to accuse him,[NOTE:2] saying, “We have experienced a lengthy time[NOTE:3] of peace through your rule,[NOTE:4] and reforms[NOTE:5] are being made in this nation[NOTE:6] through your foresight.[NOTE:7]
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Paul) has been supplied in the translation for clarity.
Or “began to bring charges, saying.”
Grk “experienced much peace.”
Grk “through you” (“rule” is implied).
This term is used only once in the NT (a hapax legomenon). It refers to improvements in internal administration (BDAG 251 s.v. διόρθωμα).
Or “being made for this people.”

References to peaceful rule, reforms, and the governor’s foresight in the opening address by Tertullus represent an attempt to praise the governor and thus make him favorable to the case. Actual descriptions of his rule portray him as inept (Tacitus, Annals 12.54; Josephus, J. W. 2.13.2-7 [2.253-270]).

verses.zh: 「腓力斯大人，我们因你得以大享太平，并且这一国的弊病，因着你的先见得以更正了；我们随时随地满心感谢不尽。
verses.en: Most excellent Felix,[NOTE:1] we acknowledge this everywhere and in every way[NOTE:2] with all gratitude.[NOTE:3]
notes: Most excellent Felix. See the note on Felix in 23:24.
Grk “in every way and everywhere.”

Or “with complete thankfulness.” BDAG 416 s.v. εὐχαριστία 1 has “μετὰ πάσης εὐ.…with all gratitude Ac 24:3.” L&N 31.26 has “‘we acknowledge this anywhere and everywhere with complete thankfulness’ Ac 24:3.”

verses.zh: 惟恐多说，你嫌烦絮，只求你宽容听我们说几句话。
verses.en: But so that I may not delay[NOTE:1] you any further, I beg[NOTE:2] you to hear us briefly[NOTE:3] with your customary graciousness.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “may not weary.” BDAG 274 s.v. ἐγκόπτω states, “ἵνα μὴ ἐπὶ πλεῖόν σε ἐγκόπτω Ac 24:4 is understood by Syr. and Armen. versions to mean in order not to weary you any further; cp. ἔγκοπος weary Diog. L. 4, 50; LXX; and ἔγκοπον ποιεῖν to weary Job 19:2; Is 43:23. But impose on is also prob.; detain NRSV.”
Or “request.”
This term is another NT hapax legomenon (BDAG 976 s.v. συντόμως 2). Tertullus was asking for a brief hearing, and implying to the governor that he would speak briefly and to the point.
BDAG 371 s.v. ἐπιείκεια has “τῇ σῇ ἐ. with your (customary) indulgence Ac 24:4.”

verses.zh: 我们看这个人，如同瘟疫一般，是鼓动普天下众犹太人生乱的，又是拿撒勒教党里的一个头目，
verses.en: For we have found[NOTE:1] this man to be a troublemaker,[NOTE:2] one who stirs up riots[NOTE:3] among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader[NOTE:4] of the sect of the Nazarenes.[NOTE:5]
notes: Grk “For having found.” The participle εὑρόντες (heurontes) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
L&N 22.6 has “(a figurative extension of meaning of λοιμός ‘plague,’ 23.158) one who causes all sorts of trouble—‘troublemaker, pest.’…‘for we have found this man to be a troublemaker” Ac 24:5.”

Or “dissensions.” While BDAG 940 s.v. στάσις 3 translates this phrase “κινεῖν στάσεις (v.l. στάσιν) τισί create dissension among certain people Ac 24:5, ” it is better on the basis of the actual results of Paul’s ministry to categorize this usage under section 2, “uprising, riot, revolt, rebellion” (cf. the use in Acts 19:40).

A ringleader. Tertullus’ basic argument was that Paul was a major disturber of the public peace. To ignore this the governor would be shunning his duty to preserve the peace and going against the pattern of his rule. In effect, Tertullus claimed that Paul was seditious (a claim the governor could not afford to ignore).tn This term is yet another NT hapax legomenon (BDAG 894 s.v. πρωτοστάτης).
The sect of the Nazarenes is a designation for followers of Jesus the Nazarene, that is, Christians.
verses.commentary:
24:5 "we have found this man" It is Luke's purpose throughout Acts to show the Roman world that
the charges against Christianity were false. This is why Luke records so many appearances before Roman
courts and officials. Paul was accused of three things:

- being a troublemaker

- being a leader of a new sect

- temple desecration

In reality the trouble makers were opponents to Paul's preaching, both pagans (i.e., Ephesus) but mostly Jews.

NASB
"a real pest"

NKJV
"a plague"

NRSV, Peshitta
"a pestilent fellow"

TEV
"a dangerous nuisance"

NJB
"a perfect pest"

REB
"a pest"

This comes from a word meaning plague (cf. Luke 21:11). In the OT (LXX) it also had the
meaning of plague, but could be used as imagery for a person (cf. Prov. 19:25).

▣ "throughout the world" This is surely a purposeful overstatement (hyperbole) and yet what
a compliment to the effectiveness of Paul's ministry in the diaspora.

▣ "ringleader" This is a compound Greek term from "first" and "to stand." It was used in
the Septuagint of Job 15:24, "a captain of the first rank." It is found only here in the NT and not at
all in the Koine papyri found in Egypt.

▣ "the sect" The term hairesis originally meant "division" or "faction" (literally,
"to make a choice'). It came to have a negative connotation, as can be seen in our English term "heresy,"
which comes from this Greek term. The Sadducees are addressed by this term in Acts 5:17 and the Pharisees
in Acts 15:5. In this context in Acts, Paul considers Christianity an integral part of the historical
Jewish faith and hope (cf. Acts 24:14). It was not a "Plan B"!

▣ "the Nazarenes" This term refers to the followers of Jesus of Nazareth. Some assert that the
term comes not from the city of Nazareth (cf. Matt. 2:23) but from nezer (BDB 666) or "branch," a title
for the Messiah (cf. Isa. 4:2; 6:13 11:1-5; 53:2; Jer. 23:5; 33:15,16; Zech. 3:8; 6:12-13).

This is the only place in the NT where believers are called by this title.

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS THE NAZARENE

verses.zh: 连圣殿他也想要污秽；我们把他捉住了。（有古卷加：要按我们的律法审问，
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] even tried to desecrate[NOTE:2] the temple, so we arrested[NOTE:3] him.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “who.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, the relative pronoun (“who”) was replaced by the third person singular pronoun (“he”) and a new sentence begun here in the translation.
Or “profane” (BDAG 173 s.v. βεβηλόω). The term was also used of profaning the Sabbath.

Or “seized.” Grk “whom also we arrested.” Because of the awkwardness of a relative clause in English at this point, the relative pronoun (“whom”) was replaced by the pronoun “him” as object of the verb.

Some mss include some material at the end of v. 6, all of 24:7, and some material at the beginning of v. 8: “and we wanted to judge him according to our law. 24:7 But Lysias the commanding officer came and took him out of our hands with a great deal of violence, 24:8 ordering those who accused him to come before you.” Acts 24:6b, 7, and 8a are lacking in P74 א A B H L P 049 81 1175 1241 pm and a few versional witnesses. They are included (with a few minor variations) in E Ψ 33 323 614 945 1505 1739 pm and a few versional witnesses. This verse (and parts of verses) is most likely not a part of the original text of Acts, for not only is it lacking from the better witnesses, there is no easy explanation as to how such could be missing from them. The present translation follows NA28 in omitting the verse number, a procedure also followed by a number of other modern translations.
verses.commentary:
24:6 Notice the charge made against Paul in Acts 21:28 that he desecrated the temple, has now
been changed to "he tried to desecrate the temple." They really had a weak case. Paul's effective
preaching was really the problem. Too many Jews, in too many synagogues were converting to Christianity.

verses.zh: 不料千夫长吕西亚前来，甚是强横，从我们手中把他夺去，吩咐告他的人到你这里来。）
verses.commentary:
24:7 The parenthesis in the NASB (i.e., part of v. 6, all of v. 7, and part of v. 8) shows a textual addition
found in the uncial MS E (8th century) and several minuscules starting the 9th century. The longer
reading is found in NKJV. It seems to change the one/ones wanting to hurt Paul from the Jewish
leadership to Lysias.

The UBS4 excludes the addition and rates the shorter version
(MSS P74, א, A, D, some Old Latin, Vulgate, Coptic, and Georgian versions) as
a "B" (almost certain). The UBS3 included the longer reading but gave it a "D" rating
(high degree of doubt). Obviously the opinions of textual scholars change!

SPECIAL TOPIC: TEXTUAL CRITICISM

verses.zh: 你自己究问他，就可以知道我们告他的一切事了。」
verses.en: When you examine[NOTE:1] him yourself, you will be able to learn from him[NOTE:2] about all these things we are accusing him of doing.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “question.”

Grk “From whom when you examine him yourself, you will be able to learn…” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, the relative pronoun (“whom”) was replaced by the third person singular pronoun (“him”) and a new sentence begun at the beginning of v. 8 in the translation.
Grk “about all these things of which we are accusing him.” This has been simplified to eliminate the relative pronoun (“of which”) in the translation.

verses.zh: 众犹太人也随着告他说：「事情诚然是这样。」
verses.en: The Jews also joined in the verbal attack,[NOTE:1] claiming[NOTE:2] that these things were true.
notes: Grk “joined in the attack,” but the adjective “verbal” has been supplied to clarify that this was not another physical assault on Paul. The verb is another NT hapax legomenon (BDAG 969 s.v. συνεπιτίθημι).
Or “asserting” (BDAG 1050 s.v. φάσκω).

verses.zh: 巡抚点头叫保罗说话。他就说：「我知道你在这国里断事多年，所以我乐意为自己分诉。
verses.en: When the governor gestured for him to speak, Paul replied, “Because I know[NOTE:1] that you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I confidently make my defense.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “knowing.” The participle ἐπιστάμενος (epistamenos) has been translated as a causal adverbial participle.
“Because…defense.” Paul also paid an indirect compliment to the governor, implying that he would be fair in his judgment.
verses.commentary:
24:10 As the attorney for the Sanhedrin used a formal introduction (probably culturally expected),
so too, does Paul.

▣ "defense" We get the English term "apology" or "apologetics" from this Greek term. It
originally meant a legal oral defense in court.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S LEGAL DEFENSE

verses.zh: 你查问就可以知道，从我上耶路撒冷礼拜到今日不过有十二天。
verses.en: As you can verify[NOTE:1] for yourself, not more than 12 days ago[NOTE:2] I went up to Jerusalem[NOTE:3] to worship.
notes: BDAG 369 s.v. ἐπιγινώσκω 2.c has “notice, perceive, learn of, ascertain…Also as legal t.t. ascertain (2 Macc 14:9) τὶ Ac 23:28; cp. 24:8. W. ὅτι foll. Ac 24:11.” “Verify” is an English synonym for “ascertain.”

Part of Paul’s defense is that he would not have had time to organize a revolt, since he had arrived in Jerusalem not more than twelve days ago.tn Grk “it is not more than twelve days from when.” This has been simplified to “not more than twelve days ago.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
24:11-12 Paul asserts that his public activities in Jerusalem were anything but abnormal and
contentious. He was accused of desecrating the temple, but in reality, he was performing an acceptable
ritual (i.e., paying for and witnessing the conclusion of a short term Nazarite vow).

verses.zh: 他们并没有看见我在殿里，或是在会堂里，或是在城里，和人辩论，耸动众人。
verses.en: They did not find me arguing[NOTE:1] with anyone or stirring up a crowd[NOTE:2] in the temple courts[NOTE:3] or in the synagogues[NOTE:4] or throughout the city,[NOTE:5]
notes: Or “disputing,” “conducting a heated discussion.”

BDAG 381 s.v. ἐπίστασις 2 has “ἐ. ποιεῖν ὄχλου to cause a crowd to gather Ac 24:12.” Roman authorities would not allow a mob to gather and threaten the peace, and anyone suspected of instigating a mob would certainly be arrested.
Grk “in the temple.” This is actually a reference to the courts surrounding the temple proper, and has been translated accordingly.
See the note on synagogue in 6:9.

A second part of Paul’s defense is that he did nothing while he was in Jerusalem to cause unrest, neither arguing nor stirring up a crowd in the temple courts or in the synagogues or throughout the city.

verses.zh: 他们现在所告我的事并不能对你证实了。
verses.en: nor can they prove[NOTE:1] to you the things[NOTE:2] they are accusing me of doing.[NOTE:3]
notes: Nor can they prove. This is a formal legal claim that Paul’s opponents lacked proof of any wrongdoing. They had no witness who could justify the arrest at the temple.tn BDAG 778 s.v. παρίστημι/παριστάνω 1.f has “οὐδὲ παραστῆσαι δύνανταί σοι περὶ ὧν νυνὶ κατηγοροῦσίν μου nor can they prove to you the accusations they are now making against me Ac 24:13.”
The words “the things” are not in the Greek text but are implied. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek when clear from the context, but must be supplied for the modern English reader.
Grk “nor can they prove to you [the things] about which they are now accusing me.” This has been simplified to eliminate the relative pronoun (“which”) in the translation.

verses.zh: 但有一件事，我向你承认，就是他们所称为异端的道，我正按着那道事奉我祖宗的　神，又信合乎律法的和先知书上一切所记载的，
verses.en: But I confess this to you, that I worship[NOTE:1] the God of our ancestors[NOTE:2] according to the Way (which they call a sect), believing everything that is according to the law[NOTE:3] and that is written in the prophets.
notes: Or “serve.”
Or “forefathers”; Grk “fathers.”

That is, the law of Moses. Paul was claiming that he legitimately worshiped the God of Israel. He was arguing that this amounted to a religious dispute rather than a political one, so that the Roman authorities need not concern themselves with it.
verses.commentary:
24:14 "I admit" See
SPECIAL TOPIC:
CONFESSION/PROFESSION

▣ "The Way" This was the early title for Christians which emphasized that Jesus is "the way"
to God (John 14:6) and a Christlike lifestyle was required (cf. Acts 9:2; 19:9,23; 22:4; 24:22 and possibly 18:25-26). See
full note at Acts 9:2.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "I do serve the God of our fathers" Paul clearly asserts in this verse that what he preaches
about Jesus in no way violates the OT. Jesus is the fulfillment of Israel's hopes and promises. He does
not see Christianity as something new and different but a fulfillment (cf. Jesus in Matt. 5:17-19). This fulfillment
theme is also carried on by the choice of "church" for the movement.

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT TITLES FOR THE SPECIAL COMING ONE

SPECIAL TOPIC: DEITY OF CHRIST FROM THE OT

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHURCH (ekklēsia)

▣ "the Law. . .the Prophets" These are two of the threefold divisions of the OT canon:

- The Torah (Law) — Genesis ‒ Deuteronomy

- The Prophets

- former prophets — Joshua ‒ Kings (except Ruth)

- latter prophets — Isaiah ‒ Malachi (except Lamentations and Daniel)

- The Writings

- Megiloth (five scrolls) — Ruth, Esther, Ecclesiastes, Song of Songs, and Lamentations

- Wisdom Literature — Job, Psalms, Proverbs

- post-exilic history — 1 and 2 Chronicles, Ezra, and Nehemiah

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW CANON

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: WISDOM LITERATURE

SPECIAL TOPIC: HISTORICAL NARRATIVE

verses.zh: 并且靠着　神，盼望死人，无论善恶，都要复活，就是他们自己也有这个盼望。
verses.en: I have[NOTE:1] a hope in God (a hope[NOTE:2] that[NOTE:3] these men[NOTE:4] themselves accept too) that there is going to be a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.[NOTE:5]
notes: Grk “having.” The participle ἔχων (echōn) has been translated as a finite verb and a new sentence begun at this point in the translation because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence.

This mention of Paul’s hope sets up his appeal to the resurrection of the dead. At this point Paul was ignoring the internal Jewish dispute between the Pharisees (to which he had belonged; Acts 23:6) and the Sadducees (who denied there would be a resurrection of the dead; Acts 23:8).

Grk “a hope in God (which these [men] themselves accept too).” Because the antecedent of the relative pronoun “which” is somewhat unclear in English, the words “a hope” have been repeated at the beginning of the parenthesis for clarity.
Grk “that they”; the referent (these men, Paul’s accusers) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
This is the only mention of the resurrection of the unrighteous in Acts. The idea parallels the idea of Jesus as the judge of both the living and the dead (Acts 10:42; 17:31).tn Or “the unjust.”
verses.commentary:
24:15 "having a hope in God which these men cherish themselves" Paul is asserting that his religious
orientation is the same as these accusers (cf. Acts 24:16), except in his view of the resurrection. Paul
is trying to defend himself by showing that the conflict is over theological issues within Judaism, which
Rome did not want to become involved with.

For "hope" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HOPE

▣ "there shall certainly be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked"
This refers to the theology of the Pharisees, not the Sadducean leadership of the temple.
Josephus, Antiq. 18.1.3, even asserts that some Pharisees denied the resurrection of
the wicked (for a modern view of annihilation see YouTube videos by Edward Fudge,
"The Fire That Consumes,"
YouTube One Hour Lecture
and Steve Gregg, "Hell: Three Christian Views"
YouTube Lecture
- 1:34:57).

The Bible is replete with this concept of a general
resurrection (cf. Isa. 25:8; Dan. 12:2; Matt. 10:15; 11:22,24; 12:41-42; 25:46; John 5:28-29; Acts 10:42; 17:31;
Rom. 2:6-11; Rev. 20:11-15; there are other texts that imply a general resurrection, cf. 1 Cor. 4:5; 5:13; 6:2; 11:32). Paul saw
Christianity as the natural fulfillment of the OT (cf. Matt. 5:17-19). It was not something new!

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGMENT IN THE NT

SPECIAL TOPIC: RESURRECTION

SPECIAL TOPIC: PHARISEES

verses.zh: 我因此自己勉励，对　神对人，常存无亏的良心。
verses.en: This is the reason[NOTE:1] I do my best to always[NOTE:2] have a clear[NOTE:3] conscience toward God and toward people.[NOTE:4]
notes: BDAG 329 s.v. ἐν 9.a, “ἐν τούτῳ πιστεύομεν this is the reason why we believe Jn 16:30; cp. Ac 24:16.”

BDAG 224 s.v. διά 2.a, “διὰ παντός…always, continually, constantly…Ac 2:25 (Ps 16:8); 10:2; 24:16.” However, the positioning of the adverb “always” in the English translation is difficult; the position used is one of the least awkward.
BDAG 125 s.v. ἀπρόσκοπος 1 has “ἀ. συνείδησις a clear conscience Ac 24:16.”
Grk “men,” but this is a generic use (Paul does not have only males in view).
verses.commentary:
24:16 "I also do my best to maintain always a blameless conscience" This same phrase is what angered
the High Priest so much in Acts 23:1-2. Paul repeats it again in his presence. It is similar to his discussion
of personal effort in 1 Cor. 9:24-27. The self-control he preached to Felix (cf. Acts 24:25) was not an
easy thing to accomplish and maintain. Self-control is one of the fruits of the Spirit in Gal. 5:22 and
possibly the capstone of the list of fruits!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSCIENCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FRUIT OF THE SPIRIT

verses.zh: 过了几年，我带着周济本国的捐项和供献的物上去。
verses.en: After several years[NOTE:1] I came to bring to my people gifts for the poor[NOTE:2] and to present offerings,[NOTE:3]
notes: BDAG 401 s.v. ἔτος has “δι᾿ ἐ. πλειόνων after several years 24:17.”
Grk “to bring alms,” but the term “alms” is not in common use today, so the closest modern equivalent, “gifts for the poor,” is used instead.

Or “sacrifices.” BDAG 887 s.v. προσφορά 1 has “προσφοράς ποιεῖν have sacrifices made Ac 24:17, ” but this may be overly specific. It is not clear from the immediate context whether the offering of sacrificial animals (so BDAG assumes) or offerings of some other sort (such as financial gifts) are in view. The combination with ἐλεημοσύνας (eleēmosunas) in the preceding clause may suggest monetary offerings. Some have suggested this is an allusion to the payments made by Paul on behalf of the four other men mentioned in Acts 21:23-26, but the text here seems to suggest something Paul had planned to do before he came, while the decision to pay for the expenses of the men in 21:23ff. was made at the suggestion of the Jerusalem leadership after he arrived. In either case, Paul was portraying himself as a pious worshiper of his God.
verses.commentary:
24:17 "I came to bring alms to my nation" This probably refers to the contribution from the Gentile
churches to the church in Jerusalem (cf. Rom. 15:25-27; 1 Cor. 16:1-4; 2 Corinthians 8-9). It is surprising
that it is not mentioned in Acts 21:15ff. This may show that it was not received well by all of the church
in Jerusalem (see James D. G. Dunn, Unity and Diversity in the New Testament). Intrenched racism
is hard to deal with even for believers.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ALMSGIVING

SPECIAL TOPIC: RACISM

▣ "and to present offerings" This refers either to

- the conclusion of Paul's limited Nazarite vow (cf. Acts 21:24)

- his paying for others' limited Nazarite vows (cf. Acts 21:24)

Because this phrase seems to be linked grammatically to "bring alms," it is possible that they
both refer to Jewish rituals, not the offerings from the churches.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAZIRITE VOW

verses.zh: 正献的时候，他们看见我在殿里已经洁净了，并没有聚众，也没有吵嚷，惟有几个从亚细亚来的犹太人。
verses.en: which I was doing when they found me in the temple, ritually purified,[NOTE:1] without a crowd or a disturbance.[NOTE:2]
notes: Ritually purified. Paul’s claim here is that he was honoring the holiness of God by being sensitive to issues of ritual purity. Not only was he not guilty of the charges against him, but he was thoroughly devout.
BDAG 458 s.v. θόρυβος 3.b has “μετὰ θορύβου…with a disturbance Ac 24:18.”
verses.commentary:
24:18 "they found me occupied in the temple, having been purified" This Jewish ritual procedure
was at the instigation of James and the elders of the church (cf. Acts 21:17-26). It was meant to placate
the legalistic Jewish believers in the church, but in reality, it inflamed the Greek-speaking Jews from Asia.

24:18-19 "Jews from Asia who ought to have been" This was an important legal point in Paul's defense
(cf. Acts 24:19). The eyewitnesses' accusers were not present! Those who were accusing Paul of worldwide
mischief had no experiential evidence (cf. Acts 24:20)!

Asia is a geographical reference to Jewish people from southern and western Turkey, then
called Asia Minor. This group of Greek speaking Jews had several synagogues in Jerusalem.

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEWS

24:19b "if" This is a FOURTH CLASS CONDITIONAL, a way to express a contingency which
is the farthest removed from possibility. A. T. Robertson, Word Pictures in the New Testament,
p. 420, calls it a mixed condition with a SECOND CLASS conclusion (i.e., but they are not
present, Acts 24:19a). His Grammar (p. 1022) lists other mixed CONDITIONAL SENTENCES in
Luke's writings (cf. Luke 17:6 and Acts 8:31).

verses.zh: 他们若有告我的事，就应当到你面前来告我。
verses.en: But there are some Jews from the province of Asia[NOTE:1] who should be here before you and bring charges,[NOTE:2] if they have anything against me.
notes: Grk “Asia”; in the NT this always refers to the Roman province of Asia. The Roman province of Asia made up about one-third of modern Asia Minor and was on the western side of it. Asia lay to the west of the region of Phrygia and Galatia. The words “the province of” are supplied to indicate to the modern reader that this does not refer to the continent of Asia.

Who should be here…and bring charges. Paul was asking, where were those who brought about his arrest and claimed he broke the law? His accusers were not really present. This subtle point raised the issue of injustice.tn BDAG 533 s.v. κατηγορέω 1 states, “nearly always as legal t.t.: bring charges in court.” L&N 33.427 states for κατηγορέω (katēgoreō), “to bring serious charges or accusations against someone, with the possible connotation of a legal or court context—‘to accuse, to bring charges.’”

verses.zh: 即或不然，这些人若看出我站在公会前，有妄为的地方，他们自己也可以说明。
verses.en: Or these men here[NOTE:1] should tell what crime[NOTE:2] they found me guilty of[NOTE:3] when I stood before the council,[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “these [men] themselves.”
Or “unrighteous act.”

The words “me guilty of” are not in the Greek text, but are implied. L&N 88.23 has “αὐτοὶ οὗτοι εἰπάτωσαν τί εὗρον ἀδίκημα στάντος μου ‘let these men themselves tell what unrighteous act they found me guilty of’ Ac 24:20.”
Grk “the Sanhedrin” (the Sanhedrin was the highest legal, legislative, and judicial body among the Jews).

verses.zh: 纵然有，也不过一句话，就是我站在他们中间大声说：『我今日在你们面前受审，是为死人复活的道理。』」
verses.en: other than[NOTE:1] this one thing[NOTE:2] I shouted out while I stood before[NOTE:3] them: ‘I am on trial before you today concerning the resurrection of the dead.’”[NOTE:4]
notes: BDAG 433 s.v. ἤ 2.c has “οὐδὲν ἕτερον ἤ nothing else than…Ac 17:21. τί…ἤ what other…than…24:21.”
Grk “one utterance.”
Cf. BDAG 327 s.v. ἐν 1.e, which has “before, in the presence of, etc.”
The resurrection of the dead. Paul’s point was, what crime was there in holding this religious belief?

verses.zh: 腓力斯本是详细晓得这道，就支吾他们说：「且等千夫长吕西亚下来，我要审断你们的事。」
verses.en: Then Felix,[NOTE:1] who understood the facts[NOTE:2] concerning the Way[NOTE:3] more accurately,[NOTE:4] adjourned their hearing,[NOTE:5] saying, “When Lysias the commanding officer comes down, I will decide your case.”[NOTE:6]
notes: See the note on Antonius Felix in 23:24.
Grk “the things.”
That is, concerning Christianity.

BDAG 39 s.v. ἀκριβῶς has “Comp. ἀκριβέστερον more exactly…ἀ. ἐκτίθεσθαι explain more exactly Ac 18:26, cp. 23:15, 20; also more accurately…24:22.” Felix knew more about the Christian movement than what the Jewish leaders had told him.

L&N 56.18 s.v. ἀναβάλλω has “to adjourn a court proceeding until a later time—‘to adjourn a hearing, to stop a hearing and put it off until later.’…‘then Felix, who was well informed about the Way, adjourned their hearing’ Ac 24:22.”
BDAG 227 s.v. διαγινώσκω 2 states, “to make a judicial decision, decide/hear (a case)…τὰ καθ᾿ ὑμᾶς decide your case Ac 24:22.”
verses.commentary:
24:22 Apparently Felix had heard about Jesus and Christianity. Probably as a Roman official he had
been briefed about the local situation to which he would be assigned.

Felix's wife was Jewish (cf. Acts 24:24), which meant he had an experiential opportunity
to know about the teaching of Judaism. The Way was considered a sect within Judaism and was, therefore,
a "legal" religion in the Roman Empire.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

verses.zh: 于是吩咐百夫长看守保罗，并且宽待他，也不拦阻他的亲友来供给他。
verses.en: He ordered the centurion[NOTE:1] to guard Paul,[NOTE:2] but to let him have some freedom,[NOTE:3] and not to prevent any of his friends[NOTE:4] from meeting his needs.[NOTE:5]
notes: See the note on the word centurion in 10:1.

Grk “that he was to be guarded.” The passive construction (τηρεῖσθαι, tēreisthai) has been converted to an active one in parallel with the following clauses, and the referent (Paul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
BDAG 77 s.v. ἄνεσις 1 states, “lit. relaxation of custodial control, some liberty, ἀ. ἔχειν have some freedom Ac 24:23.”
Grk “any of his own” (this could also refer to relatives).
Grk “from serving him.”
verses.commentary:
24:23 This shows that Felix did not see Paul as a threat and allowed some freedom and access. Here
again is a Roman official who does not sense Christianity as a political problem. This was surely one of
Luke's purposes in writing his Gospel!

verses.zh: 过了几天，腓力斯和他夫人―犹太的女子土西拉―一同来到，就叫了保罗来，听他讲论信基督耶稣的道。
verses.en: Some days later, when Felix[NOTE:1] arrived with his wife Drusilla,[NOTE:2] who was Jewish, he sent for Paul and heard him speak[NOTE:3] about faith in Christ Jesus.[NOTE:4]
notes: See the note on Antonius Felix in 23:24.

It is possible that Drusilla, being Jewish, was the source of Felix’s knowledge about the new movement called Christianity. The youngest daughter of Herod Agrippa I and sister of Agrippa II, she would have been close to 20 years old at the time. She had married the king of a small region in Syria but divorced him at the age of 16 to marry Felix. This was her second marriage and Felix’s third (Josephus, Ant. 19.9.1 [19.354], 20.7.2 [20.141-144]). As a member of Herod’s family, she probably knew about the Way.
The word “speak” is implied; BDAG 32 s.v. ἀκούω 1.c has “ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ περὶ τῆς…πίστεως he heard him speak about faith Ac 24:24.”
Or “Messiah Jesus”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”
verses.commentary:
24:24 "Drusilla" She was the youngest, and apparently beautiful, daughter of Herod Agrippa I and
the sister of Bernice and Agrippa II. She was Felix's third wife, whom he took from the Azizus, the King
of Emesa (cf. Josephus, Antiq. 20.7.2).

NASB, NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB
"Christ Jesus"

NKJV
"Christ"

Peshitta
"the Christian Faith"

Option #1 is found in MSS P74, א*,
B, E, and the Old Latin, Vulgate versions. The shorter reading is found in MSS
אc, A, C, and the Peshitta and Coptic versions. The
UBS4 gives the longer version a "B" rating (almost certain).

One wonders if in this context "Christ" should be translated "Messiah" (MS 044 has
"the Messiah").

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

▣ "faith" This is a crucial theological word. Remember these theological terms in Koine Greek
are based not on Greek usage, but the Septuagint, the Koine Greek translation of the Hebrew Scriptures. Luke knew
the Septuagint well. It was the OT translation used in the Greek speaking synagogues for the early church.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTAUGINT

24:24-25 Paul preached the gospel often (cf. Acts 24:26b) to Felix and Drusilla. This was exactly
what Jesus wanted him to do (cf. Acts 9:15). He was convicted, but also greedy (i.e., he wanted Paul to
bribe him) and kept putting off his legal decision (cf. Acts 24:26).

verses.zh: 保罗讲论公义、节制，和将来的审判。腓力斯甚觉恐惧，说：「你暂且去吧，等我得便再叫你来。」
verses.en: While Paul[NOTE:1] was discussing[NOTE:2] righteousness, self-control,[NOTE:3] and the coming judgment, Felix[NOTE:4] became[NOTE:5] frightened and said, “Go away for now, and when I have an opportunity,[NOTE:6] I will send for you.”
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Paul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “speaking about.”

The topic of self-control was appropriate in view of the personal history of both Felix and Drusilla (see the note on “Drusilla” in the previous verse), and might well account for Felix’s anxiety.tn Grk “and self-control.” This καί (kai) has not been translated since English normally uses a coordinating conjunction only between the last two elements in a series of three or more.
See the note on Felix in 23:26.
Grk “becoming.” The participle γενόμενος (genomenos) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
Or “when I find time.” BDAG 639 s.v. μεταλαμβάνω 2 has “καιρὸν μ. have an opportunity = find time…Ac 24:25.”

verses.zh: 腓力斯又指望保罗送他银钱，所以屡次叫他来，和他谈论。
verses.en: At the same time he was also hoping that Paul would give him money,[NOTE:1] and for this reason he sent for Paul[NOTE:2] as often as possible[NOTE:3] and talked[NOTE:4] with him.
notes: Grk “he was hoping that money would be given to him by Paul.” To simplify the translation, the passive construction has been converted to an active one.sn Would give him money. That is, would offer him a bribe in exchange for his release. Such practices were fairly common among Roman officials of the period (Josephus, Ant. 2.12.3 [2.272-274]).
Grk “him”; the referent (Paul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

“As often as possible” reflects the comparative form of the adjective πυκνός (puknos); see BDAG 897 s.v. πυκνός, which has “Neut. of the comp. πυκνότερον as adv. more often, more frequently and in an elative sense very often, quite frequently…also as often as possible…Ac 24:26.”
On this term, which could mean “conferred with him,” see BDAG 705 s.v. ὁμιλέω.
verses.commentary:
24:26 Apparently Paul had some funds during this prison period. Possibly from (1) a personal
inheritance or (2) help from the churches (i.e., Philippi or Thessalonica). Felix called for Paul often,
not to hear him speak, but in hopes of receiving a bribe.

verses.zh: 过了两年，波求•非斯都接了腓力斯的任；腓力斯要讨犹太人的喜欢，就留保罗在监里。
verses.en: After two years[NOTE:1] had passed, Porcius Festus[NOTE:2] succeeded Felix,[NOTE:3] and because he wanted to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in prison.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “After a two-year period.”

Porcius Festus was the procurator of Palestine who succeeded Felix; neither the beginning nor the end of his rule (at his death) can be determined with certainty, although he appears to have died in office after about two years. Nero recalled Felix in a.d. 57 or 58, and Festus was appointed to his vacant office in a.d. 57, 58, or 59. According to Josephus (Ant. 20.8.9-10 [20.182-188]; J. W. 2.14.1 [2.271-272]), his administration was better than that of his predecessor Felix or his successor Albinus, but Luke in Acts portrays him in a less favorable light: He was willing to sacrifice Paul to court Jewish favor by taking him to Jerusalem for trial (see 25:9), regardless of Paul’s guilt or innocence. The one characteristic for which Festus was noted is that he dealt harshly with those who disturbed the peace.
Grk “Felix received as successor Porcius Festus.”sn See the note on Felix in 23:26.
Grk “left Paul imprisoned.”sn Felix left Paul in prison. Luke makes the point that politics got in the way of justice here; keeping Paul in prison was a political favor to the Jews.
verses.commentary:
24:27 "after two years had passed" Many believe that it was during this period that Luke gathered
eyewitness information from those in Palestine for his Gospel (cf. Luke 1:1-4). This must have been a
discouraging time to an aggressive man like Paul! However, he did not seek freedom by means of bribery. He
knew he was in God's will (i.e., Eph. 6:18-19).

▣ "Porcius Festus" There is some disagreement between the Roman historians, Suetonius and
Tacitus, over the beginning date of his office. Felix was put on trial in A.D. 55, but it
is uncertain whether he was convicted and removed then or in A.D. 59. Festus died in
A.D. 62, while still in office (cf. Josephus, Antiq. 20.9.1). There is little known
about him (cf. Josephus, Antiq. 20.8.9-10; Wars 2.14.1).

▣ "Felix left Paul imprisoned" It was customary to release all the prisoners at the time
of the change of administrations. This verse shows the political situation in Palestine and the weakness
of the Roman leaders, as well as the power of the Sanhedrin.
